deep.reconstruction:
HEADING. 'Mo- natl. Sell.' are faint pencil notes, probably a reference to the Monatliche Correspondenz. Then 'Litt. Ff.'.

DEFINITION. Gauss writes {α,β,n} = P = 1 + αβ/(1·n) x + α(α+1)β(β+1)/(1·2·n(n+1)) x² + … . In modern notation this is the Gauss hypergeometric series 2F1(α,β;n;x). Here the third parameter is called n. In the differential equation further down it is called γ.

CONTIGUOUS RELATIONS. Write F = F(α,β;n;x) and F⁺ = F(α+1,β+1;·;x).
(1) F(α,β;n+1) = F(α,β;n) − αβx/(n(n+1)) · F(α+1,β+1;n+2).
(2) F(α,β+1;n) = F(α,β;n) + (αx/n) · F(α+1,β+1;n+1).
(3) F(α,β+1;n+1) = F(α,β;n) + α(n−β)x/(n(n+1)) · F(α+1,β+1;n+2).
'Also' (therefore):
(4) (n−β)·F(α,β;n+1) + β·F(α,β+1;n+1) = n·F(α,β;n). Gauss overwrote the third argument to n+1.
  - Derivation (implicit; mine): multiply (1) by (n−β) and (3) by β and add. The F(α+1,β+1;n+2) terms cancel.
(5) F(α,β+1;n) = F(α+1,β;n) + (α−β)x/n · F(α+1,β+1;n+1).
  - Derivation (mine): (2) minus its α↔β analogue F(α+1,β;n) = F + (βx/n)F⁺.
(6) A first attempt is struck out. The rewritten version is β·F(α,β+1;n) = α·F(α+1,β;n) − (α−β)·F(α,β;n), marked 'gut'.
  - Derivation (mine): α×[F(α+1,β) = F + (βx/n)F⁺] minus β×(2). The F⁺ terms cancel.

DIFFERENTIAL EQUATION. 'Kommt in die DG' (substitute into the differential equation). The equation is written in Leibniz differentials, valid for an arbitrary independent variable:
(x−x²)d²P − (x−x²)dP·d²x/dx + {γ−(α+β+1)x}dP·dx − αβP·dx² = 0 (the '=0' is implicit).
This is the hypergeometric equation x(1−x)P_xx + [γ−(α+β+1)x]P_x − αβP = 0. The second term turns d²P into the correct second derivative when t is the independent variable, since d²P/dx² = (d²P − dP·d²x/dx)/dx².

SUBSTITUTION A: x = t/(t−1) (Pfaff/Euler type).
- dx = −dt/(t−1)².
- d²x = 2dt²/(t−1)³.
- x − x² = −t/(t−1)².
The terms of the equation become:
- −t/(t−1)² P''.
- −2t/(t−1)³ P'.
- {γ − (α+β+1)t/(t−1)}·P'·(−1/(t−1)²).
- −αβP/(t−1)⁴.
Gauss begins to clear denominators: 't(t−1)²P'' − (t−1)P'' …' and '(t−tt)P'' − P'{γ(t−1) …'. He then breaks off.
Completed by me: (t−t²)P'' − P'{γ(t−1) + (1−α−β)t} − αβP/(t−1) = 0. This is not hypergeometric in P itself. One needs P = (1−t)^α Q, giving Pfaff's F(α,β;γ;t/(t−1)) = (1−t)^α F(α,γ−β;γ;t), which presumably is why he abandons it.

MARGIN. 'y, 1−yy, 1−xyy' points to the elliptic integral ∫dy/√((1−y²)(1−xy²)), i.e. the Landen/AGM context.

SUBSTITUTION B: x = 4t/(1+t)² (quadratic / Landen transformation).
Gauss writes:
- dx = 4(1−t)dt/(1+t)³.
- ddx = 8(2−t)dt²/(1+t)⁴.
- x − xx = (1−t)²/(1+t)⁴.
The scratch '−1−t, −3+3t' is the computation of d²x.
He substitutes and gets:
(1−t)²/(1+t)⁴ P'' + (1−t)(4−2t)/(1+t)⁵ P' + {γ − (α+β+1)·4t/(1+t)²}·4(1−t)/(1+t)³ P' − 16αβ(1−t)²/(1+t)⁶ P.
Multiplying by (1+t)⁴/(1−t) gives his final line:
(1−t)P'' + P'/(1+t)·{4γ(1+t)² + 4 − 2t(8α+8β+9)} − 16αβ(1−t)P/(1+t)².
Here 4 − 2t − 16t(α+β+1) = 4 − 2t(8α+8β+9).

Corrected version (mine), using x − x² = 4t(1−t)²/(1+t)⁴ and d²x = −8(2−t)dt²/(1+t)⁴:
t(1−t)P'' + P'/(1+t)·{2t(2−t) + γ(1+t)² − 4t(α+β+1)} − 4αβ(1−t)P/(1+t)² = 0.
This is the step toward the quadratic transformation F(α,β;2β;4t/(1+t)²) = (1+t)^{2α} F(α, α−β+½; β+½; t²). It underlies the AGM/Landen relation.

PURPOSE. The page prepares the contiguous relations used for the continued fraction on the next page, and explores which changes of variable map the hypergeometric equation to itself.
errors: d²x for x = 4t/(1+t)² is −8(2−t)dt²/(1+t)⁴, not +8(2−t)dt²/(1+t)⁴. The margin scratch (−1−t−3+3t = 2t−4) actually gives the negative sign. In the P' term the sign comes out right anyway (+(1−t)(4−2t)/(1+t)⁵).

x − xx for x = 4t/(1+t)² is 4t(1−t)²/(1+t)⁴. Gauss drops the factor 4t. This propagates into the P'' coefficient and into the d²x-term contribution to P'. His final reduced equation is therefore wrong: P'' should have coefficient t(1−t) after dividing by 4, and the '4−2t' term should be 4t(4−2t) before dividing by 4.
Pfaff substitution: dP·dx = P'·(−dt/(t−1)²), so the γ-term carries a factor −1/(t−1)². The page appears to show +1/(t−1)²; the sign is restored in the next line '−P'{γ(t−1)…'.
The Pfaff computation is left incomplete. As written, P itself does not satisfy a hypergeometric equation in t (a term αβP/(t−1) remains) unless one sets P = (1−t)^α Q.
The equation is written without '= 0'. The third parameter is called n in the series and γ in the differential equation (notational inconsistency, not an error).

results.what: Contiguous relations (1)–(6) for 2F1(α,β;n;x), e.g. nF(α,β;n) = (n−β)F(α,β;n+1) + βF(α,β+1;n+1) and (α−β)F = αF(α+1) − βF(β+1)
results.modern_name: Gauss contiguous relations of the hypergeometric function
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss, Disquisitiones generales circa seriem infinitam (1812/1813)

results.what: Hypergeometric ODE written in differentials so that an arbitrary change of independent variable can be made
results.modern_name: hypergeometric differential equation under change of variable
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (ODE); Gauss's posthumous 'Determinatio seriei nostrae per aequationem differentialem' (Werke III)

results.what: Substitution x = t/(t−1) into the hypergeometric ODE (left incomplete)
Substitution x = 4t/(1+t)² into the hypergeometric ODE (with slips), in the elliptic-integral/Landen context
results.usually_credited_to: Kummer (1836) for systematic treatment; Gauss posthumously (Werke III), Landen for the elliptic case

deep.surprise_reason: The contiguous relations are exactly those of Gauss's 1812 memoir, and quadratic transformations of 2F1 tied to the AGM appear in his posthumous Nachlass (Werke III). This page is a working draft of known Gauss material, with computational slips in the quadratic substitution. Its main interest is as evidence of the early dating (around 1805) of the drafts.

transcription_corrections: In (4) the last braces are {α,β+1,n+1}; Gauss overwrote the original n with n+1.
In (6) the parentheses (α+1,β,n) should be braces {α+1,β,n}, the same function.
'Kommt in der DG.' is more plausibly 'Kommt in die DG.' (substitution into the differential equation).
The Pfaff γ-term should carry the factor −1/(t−1)²; the page shows 1/(t−1)², a sign slip in Gauss's own working.
The line '−t/(t−1)² P'' + t/(t−1)² · 2/(t−1)³ · (t−1)…' is Gauss's first attempt at the d²x term. It is superseded by '−2t/(t−1)³ P''.

In the quadratic substitution the P' coefficient reads (1−t)(4−2t)/(1+t)⁵, with a struck-out first numerator. The final line reads {4γ(1+t)² + 4 − 2t(8α+8β+9)}, with the auxiliary '4−2t' and '4γ(1+t)² − 16t(α+β+1)' written above it.
